items.rationale: The model keeps nothing between calls. The program appends each output and tool result to the message list and sends the whole list again, so the earlier call is in the input.

Call k receives 1,000 + (k - 1) x 400 tokens: 1,000, 1,400, 1,800, 2,200, 2,600, which sum to 9,000. By formula, nB + a n(n-1)/2 = 5,000 + 400 x 10 = 9,000. An answer of 3,000 or 7,000 counts only the last call or ignores the repeated history.

Training permission is a safety decision and rests on the authoritative record, read through a tool at the moment of the decision. A saved note is a copy that can be stale, and the student's word is a claim. Waiting for notes to refresh still relies on a note instead of the record.

Retrieval adds only the few relevant chunks, so the context stays small and each call stays cheap while the needed passage is present. The whole manual is re-billed on every call, a summary can drop the setting needed, and training knowledge may not match this machine.

items.answer: clear the old tool result from the history, or summarize the history (compaction)
accepted: remove the old tool result from the history
summarize it and start a fresh context
give the task to a sub-agent
items.rationale: The raw result is re-sent and re-billed on every later call and can reduce recall. Clearing it, summarizing the history (compaction), or keeping such work in a sub-agent with its own context removes it from the main context.
